config.title: Conditional Rendering with Ternary

intro.title: Conditional Rendering with Ternary
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build a dynamic React component that displays different content based on user conditions, such as showing a welcome message for logged-in users or a login prompt for guests. You'll learn conditional rendering, a fundamental React concept that allows components to display different UI elements based on the application's state or props. The core programming construct you'll master is the ternary operator (condition ? trueValue : falseValue), which provides a concise way to handle conditional logic directly within JSX. You'll work with React functional components, JSX syntax, and state management using the useState hook. By the end of this lesson, you'll understand how to create responsive user interfaces that adapt their content dynamically based on different conditions.
intro.usecase: Conditional rendering with ternary operators is essential for creating dynamic user interfaces that respond to user state and interactions. You'll see this pattern everywhere in modern web apps: showing login vs logout buttons based on authentication status, displaying loading spinners while data fetches, toggling between edit and view modes in forms, and showing different dashboard content based on user permissions. E-commerce sites use ternaries to show 'Add to Cart' vs 'Out of Stock' buttons, while social media platforms conditionally render follow/unfollow buttons and private/public content. This pattern is so fundamental that virtually every React component in production apps uses ternary operators to create responsive, state-driven user experiences.

objectives: Implement ternary operators to conditionally render JSX elements based on boolean values
Apply conditional logic to control the display of different components within a React application
Construct inline conditional expressions that render alternative content based on state variables
Configure component rendering behavior by evaluating props through ternary conditions
Manipulate UI visibility by combining multiple ternary operators for complex conditional scenarios
Initialize conditional rendering patterns that respond to user interactions and state changes
Integrate ternary expressions with event handlers to update displayed content dynamically

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and useState from 'react' at the top of your file.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: importing multiple items from a library
import { Component, useState } from 'react'
steps.expectedOutcome: React and useState are imported and available for use in the component.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure you're importing both React and useState from the 'react' package.
steps.feedbackWrong: import both React and useState from 'react' using the import statement.

steps.title: Create the main App component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that returns JSX
steps.hint: Start with 'function App()' or 'const App = () =>' and include a return statement with JSX
steps.expectedOutcome: A functional component named App that returns JSX structure
successCriteria: App component is created and returns JSX
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your App component returns some JSX content.
steps.feedbackWrong: create a component named 'App' that returns JSX. You can use either function declaration or arrow function syntax.

steps.title: Initialize state for conditional visibility
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, initialize state using useState with a variable named 'isVisible' set to an initial value of true.
steps.hint: Use useState(true) and destructure it into isVisible and a setter function. Place this at the top of your component function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: initializing boolean state
const [isOpen, setIsOpen] = useState(false)
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a state variable 'isVisible' initialized to true, managed by useState hook.
successCriteria: The useState hook is used to create an 'isVisible' state variable with initial value true and its corresponding setter function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure you're using useState to create both the isVisible variable and its setter function, with true as the initial value.
steps.feedbackWrong: use the useState hook with true as the initial value, and destructure it into isVisible and its setter function (commonly named setIsVisible).

steps.title: Define toggle handler function
steps.instruction: Create a function named toggleVisibility that toggles the isVisible state between true and false using setIsVisible
steps.hint: Use setIsVisible with the previous state value (prevState) and return the opposite boolean value using !prevState
steps.expectedOutcome: A toggleVisibility function is defined that uses setIsVisible to toggle the boolean state
successCriteria: toggleVisibility function is created and uses setIsVisible to toggle the isVisible state
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your function uses setIsVisible to toggle the boolean value of isVisible.
steps.feedbackWrong: The toggle function should use setIsVisible with a callback that returns the opposite of the previous state (!prevState).

steps.title: Add container div element
steps.instruction: Inside the return statement of your App component, add a div element with the text 'Welcome to Conditional Rendering' as its content.
steps.hint: Replace the empty div in the return statement with a div that contains the welcome text.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: a div with text content
Hello World
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now renders a div containing welcome text about conditional rendering.
successCriteria: A div element contains the text 'Welcome to Conditional Rendering'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure the div contains the exact text 'Welcome to Conditional Rendering'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The div should contain the text 'Welcome to Conditional Rendering'. Check that you've added the text inside the div element.

steps.title: Add toggle button with click handler
steps.instruction: Add a button element with the text 'Toggle Content' that calls the toggleVisibility function when clicked.
steps.hint: Use the onClick attribute to wire the button to your toggleVisibility handler function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: button with click handler
<button onClick={handleClick}>Click Me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button with 'Toggle Content' text that triggers the toggleVisibility function when clicked
successCriteria: Button element is added with text 'Toggle Content' and onClick handler set to toggleVisibility
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your button has the text 'Toggle Content' and the onClick attribute calls toggleVisibility.
steps.feedbackWrong: add a button element with onClick={toggleVisibility} and the text 'Toggle Content'.

steps.title: Add conditional content using ternary operator
steps.instruction: Below the button, add a paragraph that uses the ternary operator to conditionally display 'Content is visible!' when isVisible is true, and null when false.
steps.hint: Use the ternary syntax: condition ? valueIfTrue : valueIfFalse. Place it inside JSX curly braces.
steps.expectedOutcome: A paragraph that conditionally renders 'Content is visible!' when isVisible is true, using the ternary operator.
successCriteria: A ternary operator is used to conditionally render a paragraph with 'Content is visible!' based on the isVisible state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start with the ternary operator! Make sure you're checking the isVisible state and rendering the paragraph with the correct text.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ternary operator needs the format: condition ? valueIfTrue : valueIfFalse. Use isVisible as the condition and render a paragraph when true.

steps.title: Add content for the visible state
steps.instruction: Add a paragraph element inside the ternary operator that displays 'Content is visible!' when the condition is true
steps.hint:
Replace the comment inside the ternary with a

element containing the text 'Content is visible!'
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: showing content in a ternary {showWelcome ?

Welcome back!

: null}
steps.expectedOutcome: A paragraph element with the text 'Content is visible!' appears inside the ternary operator for the true condition
successCriteria: A paragraph element containing 'Content is visible!' is added as the true branch of the ternary operator
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure you're adding a paragraph element with the exact text 'Content is visible!' in the true branch of the ternary.
steps.feedbackWrong:
Not quite right. You need to add a

element with the text 'Content is visible!' where the comment is located in the ternary operator.

steps.title: Add content for the hidden state
steps.instruction: Update the ternary operator to show a paragraph with the text 'Content is hidden' instead of null when isVisible is false
steps.hint: Replace 'null' in the false branch of the ternary with a paragraph element containing the hidden state message.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: ternary with content for both branches {isLoggedIn ?

Welcome back!

:

Please log in

}
steps.expectedOutcome: The ternary operator now displays different content for both true and false conditions
successCriteria: The false branch of the ternary displays a paragraph with 'Content is hidden' text instead of null
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure to replace null with a paragraph element that contains the text 'Content is hidden'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ternary operator should have a paragraph with 'Content is hidden' text in the false branch instead of null.

steps.title: Export the App component
steps.instruction: Add an export default statement to make the App component available as the default export
steps.hint: Use 'export default' followed by the component name to export it as the default export from this module
steps.analogousExample:
// Export a component as default
export default MyComponent
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is exported as the default export, making it available for import in other files
successCriteria: The App component is exported as the default export using 'export default App'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track with exporting, but make sure to use 'export default' followed by the component name.
steps.feedbackWrong: add an export statement. Use 'export default App' to make your component available as the default export.
